__README__: === WORKFLOW C: User Notification (Email via SES) === This workflow runs after Workflow B completes matching. It fetches all new matches for the batch, groups them by user, builds a personalized email listing the loan products they qualify for, and sends it via AWS SES. IMPORTANT NOTES FOR THE DEMO: 1. Do NOT email the sample CSV addresses (they're fake). 2. Use test-inbox aliases: yourname+one@gmail.com, yourname+two@gmail.com 3. In SES sandbox mode, you must verify both sender AND receiver email addresses. 4. Show one received email in the demo video. TRIGGER: Webhook — called by Workflow B after saving matches.
name: Workflow C - Email Notifications

nodes.name: Webhook Trigger
nodes.notes: WHAT: Listens for POST requests at /webhook/notification-trigger. WHO CALLS IT: Workflow B, after saving all matches to the database. WHAT DATA IT RECEIVES: { batch_id: 'abc-123' }. WHY A SEPARATE WORKFLOW: The task defines three separate workflows (A, B, C). Keeping C separate means you can test email sending independently.

parameters.query:
-- Fetch all un-notified matches for this batch, with user and product details.
-- We JOIN all three tables to get everything we need in one query:
-- - User's name and email (for the email)
-- - Product name, provider, interest rate (for the email content)
-- - Match score and reason (for personalization)
--
-- WHERE notified = FALSE: Only get matches we haven't emailed yet.
-- This prevents duplicate emails if the workflow runs again.
--
-- ORDER BY: Group by user so we can aggregate all products per user.
SELECT
    m.match_id,
    m.user_id,
    m.match_score,
    m.match_reason,
    u.name AS user_name,
    u.email AS user_email,
    lp.product_name,
    lp.provider,
    lp.interest_rate
FROM matches m
JOIN users u ON m.user_id = u.user_id
JOIN loan_products lp ON m.product_id = lp.product_id
WHERE m.batch_id = '{{ $json.body.batch_id }}'
  AND m.notified = FALSE
ORDER BY u.user_id, m.match_score DESC;

nodes.name: Fetch Unnotified Matches
nodes.notes: WHAT: Queries all matches for this batch that haven't been emailed yet. WHY JOIN 3 TABLES: We need data from users (name, email), loan_products (product details), and matches (score, reason) — all in one query to minimize database round-trips. WHY ORDER BY user_id: So the next Code node can group products by user efficiently.

nodes.name: Group Matches & Build Email HTML
nodes.notes: WHAT: Groups all matches by user (so each user gets ONE email with all their matched products) and builds a styled HTML email. WHY GROUP: Without grouping, a user matched to 5 products would get 5 separate emails. That's spammy. One email with a table is professional. WHY HTML EMAIL: A plain text email would work, but an HTML email with a product table looks much better in the demo video. LIMIT: We cap at 5 emails because SES sandbox mode has a daily sending limit of ~200 emails.

nodes.name: Send Email via AWS SES
nodes.notes: WHAT: Sends the personalized email via AWS Simple Email Service (SES). SETUP REQUIRED: 1. In AWS Console → SES → Verify your sender email address 2. In SES Sandbox mode, also verify receiver addresses 3. In n8n, create AWS credentials (access key + secret key) 4. Replace 'your-verified-email@gmail.com' with your verified sender SES SANDBOX: By default, SES is in sandbox mode which only allows sending to VERIFIED email addresses. For the demo, verify your test addresses (yourname+one@gmail.com, yourname+two@gmail.com) in the SES console. EXPRESSIONS: {{ $json.to_email }} = the recipient from the Code node. {{ $json.subject }} = the personalized subject line. {{ $json.html_body }} = the HTML email content.

parameters.query:
-- Mark all matches for this user as notified so we don't email them again.
-- We use the match_ids array from the Code node to update specific rows.
UPDATE matches
SET notified = TRUE
WHERE match_id = ANY(ARRAY[{{ $json.match_ids.join(',') }}]::INTEGER[]);

nodes.name: Mark Matches as Notified
nodes.notes: WHAT: Sets notified=TRUE for all matches we just emailed. WHY: Prevents duplicate emails. If Workflow C runs again (e.g., retry after a partial failure), it only processes matches where notified=FALSE. HOW: Uses PostgreSQL's ANY() function with an array of match IDs. The expression {{ $json.match_ids.join(',') }} converts the JavaScript array [1,2,3] into the SQL-friendly string '1,2,3'.
